children: Greenland Resources said it is in favor of the defense agreement with Greenland, Denmark and the U.S., which it believes will strengthen security and encourage investment.
The deal will benefit the people of Greenland by supporting a sustainable long-term supply of minerals for end users, said the Canadian mining company, which operates in Greenland.

On Friday, President Trump said the U.S. and Denmark reached a deal to allow more American forces in Greenland. Denmark, which has sovereignty over the island, will allow the U.S. to have a permanent military presence and increase the number of bases there.
Greenland Resources operates the Malmbjerg mine in Greenland, where it produces molybdenum. It has several binding long-term agreements with major global steel companies.
Shares of the company rose 12% to $1.84 on Monday. The stock is up 29% this year.
